The research phase ran 06:00-06:48 ET of a ~60 minute budget and closed with a RESEARCH COMPLETE block (the 06:48 block supersedes an earlier 06:39 one, which it corrected after adding SIRI). WHAT THIS REPORT IS. Seven of the eight ideas are decisions on money already at risk, which is what prior context puts first: one CLOSE (BCC), two ACTs (HII, a stop set on the book's largest unprotected gain; ACM, trim half into tomorrow's print), and four flagged or disciplined holds (OXY, AAL, TLT, and SIRI as the one genuinely new-risk accumulation bid). Even DKS is not new: a BUY @ 144.50 was published 2026-11-13 and still awaits entry, so today's row amends that pending order at an unchanged level rather than opening a second position — the research log called DKS "the best new idea of the run", which overstates it. All 14 open positions were reviewed. KHC, UNP, ABT, PYPL, RTX and XLU are unchanged holds needing no row (all above both moving averages with stops below both). Four dead pending orders are cancelled on the watchlist: GLD SELL @ 406.77, /MBTZ6 SHORT @ 74,075, CVS BUY @ 79.00 and the stale September CPI contract.

RANK 1 IS AN EXIT, NOT THE BEST BUY. Ranking is conviction, then reward-to-risk, then catalyst proximity, and BCC tops it as a conviction-5 immediate close. Two actions are dated for Monday 2026-11-16 regardless of rank: close BCC at the open, and trim half of ACM into the after-close earnings print (rank 6).

WHY THE REPORT IS THIN, AND IT IS A MARKET CONDITION RATHER THAN A SHORTFALL. Four independent floor tests failed the same way. XLP, XLV, XLE and XLF are all leading groups sitting 1-7% off their 120-day highs with ATRs wide enough that an honest 1.8-ATR stop pushes a 2:1 target above the range high — XLP needs 95.41 against a 93.40 high, XLV needs 196.95 against 192.32. Meanwhile the de-rated names (BCC, LEN, CVS, ADM, HUN, CAG) have no insider support: one buyer each at most, and CVS carries 352.7M USD of insider selling. About 36 names were insider-screened and exactly one genuine officer cluster turned up, DKS, whose seven buyers are named natural persons. Two names that screened better on raw counts were disqualified by reading the buyer NAMES rather than the distinct-buyer count: ENR's 41 buys and 19.3M USD are all "Aqua Capital, Ltd." (a fund) and LEN's 24 are a single filer. SIRI's three are Berkshire Hathaway — a real signal, but one institution, and the idea says so instead of calling it insider buying.

BOTH WEEKEND LANES WERE CLOSED BY DATA OUTAGES, NOT BY CHOICE. Event contracts returned ok with count 0 on all nine topics tried (Fed, CPI, bitcoin, inflation, recession, "Bitcoin price", "S&P", election, GDP), so no event contract could be priced without inventing a cents entry. And no crypto OHLC history is obtainable — there is no `crypto history` subcommand and yahoo rate-limited BTC-USD all run — so no crypto stop could be checked against the 2.5-ATR floor. BTC 65,527 (-2.56%), ETH 1,829.42 (-4.12%) and SOL 72.08 (-4.80%) were fetched as spot, but no crypto idea was published rather than invent an ATR. On a Sunday those are the two lanes strategy.md leans on, which is why this run carries equity week-ahead prep instead.

PRICES AND SESSION. US equities and futures were closed. Every price is the Friday 2026-11-13 close, re-quoted during synthesis and unchanged, with session "closed" and age ~2317 minutes — a closed market, not stale data. Every equity level here is for the NEXT open, Monday 2026-11-16.

SOURCES THAT FAILED. `market_data.py macro` timed out twice (120s and 300s, no output), so the actual 10y/2y yield levels, the VIX index itself, DXY and every FRED series are UNVERIFIED and are asserted nowhere — the levels block carries them as null and uses VIXY and UUP only as named ETF proxies. Also failed: yahoo (429 on all history), yahoo-options (401, so no target was checked against an options-implied move, DKS's included), stooq (connect timeout), and the nasdaq short-interest endpoint (ReadTimeout, so no squeeze claim is made for DKS). Worked: finnhub quotes/earnings/insiders/analysts, nasdaq equity history for ATR and moving averages, SEC filings, CoinGecko spot. Not reached as deliberate lanes: micro caps, FDA calendars, index rebalances, lockup unlocks.

THREE IDEAS KNOWINGLY CARRY DEFECTS, ALL DISCLOSED RATHER THAN PATCHED. (1) AAL's 14.40 stop is 1.71 ATR from the 13.35 entry, inside the 2.0 swing floor — recomputed here from a fetched ATR14 of 0.6129. It is inherited from an entry made 2026-10-03 and was NOT widened, because widening a stop to clear a floor on a position already open is the KRE error this report has shipped before; validation should flag it and demoting it is the correct outcome. (2) HII's `risk_reward` is published as null because the 278.50 stop sits ABOVE the 262.00 entry, making any entry-measured ratio meaningless — risk from the fill is negative. Measured from Friday's 306.24, the only honest frame for a position being managed, it is 33.52 of upside against 27.74 of downside, 1.21:1, whose break-even hit rate is 0.452 — so the 0.55 win probability is a ten-point edge claim, not the thirty-plus an entry-measured calculation would wrongly imply. (3) BCC carries no target, no stop and no ratio because it is an exit instruction and not a trade; no reward-to-risk can be computed for closing a position, and none is claimed. It will fail the mechanical downside checks for exactly that reason.

ON THE RATIOS CLUSTERED JUST ABOVE THE FLOOR, WHICH THIS REPORT IS TOLD TO DISTRUST. Three of the six computable ratios sit at 2.00, 2.00 and 2.08 against a 2.0 swing floor (ACM, DKS, OXY) — the signature of targets nudged until they pass. Every ratio was recomputed here from the final entry, target and stop, and every stop was re-checked in ATRs against a freshly fetched ATR14, which is the test the ratio cannot answer: ACM 2.41 ATR, DKS 2.58, OXY 2.09, SIRI 2.01, TLT 1.97 against the 1.8 ETF floor. The stops are on the conservative side of the floor rather than walked in, and the levels on all three are unchanged from the original entries rather than refitted. Two mid-run self-corrections in the log support that reading rather than undercutting it. ACM: research first proposed tightening the stop from 61.50 to 64.50 as prudence, which would have sat 1.03 ATR from entry — inside the floor the original stop already cleared at 2.41 — and would have lifted reward-to-risk from 2.00 to 4.68 purely by moving the stop closer; it was superseded, and on a position in profit "raise the stop" is not automatically the conservative choice. SIRI: the 2.0-ATR stop computed to 26.0868 and was first written 26.09, which rounded TOWARD the entry and left it at 1.997 ATR, fractionally inside the floor; corrected to 26.08 at 2.0065 ATR. Round a stop away from the entry, never toward it.

CONVICTION SCORES WERE CORRECTED UPWARD BY ONE, MECHANICALLY. Research scored conviction as the raw count of distinct evidence kinds; strategy.md and validate_report.py both map 4+ kinds to 5, 3 kinds to 4, 2 kinds to 3 and 1 kind to 2. Applying that table raised six scores (BCC and DKS 4 to 5; ACM, AAL, OXY and SIRI 3 to 4) and left TLT and HII at 3. No evidence was added or reworded to achieve it, and the count is auditable against each idea's `evidence` array. Position sizes are unchanged from research — 2% standard, 3% HII, 0% for the BCC exit — because conviction counts confirmations and does not authorise more size, and because six of the eight are existing positions rather than new allocations. Note that conviction 5 has no closed trades in the record yet.

CORRELATION IS INSIDE THE CAP, WITH ONE THING TO WATCH. No driver carries more than two ideas: rate path TLT (long duration) and BCC (building products), and consumer DKS long against AAL short, which point opposite ways. The watch item is the calendar rather than the book — this is retail-earnings week bracketed by NVDA Tuesday after the close, with HD and DIS Tuesday, TGT/LOW/TJX/ROST Wednesday and WMT/BABA Thursday, so one consumer print could move DKS on sympathy. DKS is the only new consumer exposure added, deliberately.

TRACK-RECORD CAUTION, NOT OVER-FITTED. long_term is 0/4 and conviction-2 is 0/6, both far under the ~15-trade threshold, so they are noise. No long_term idea is published because no valuation anchor was defensible inside the research budget, and no conviction-2 idea because nothing thin enough to be a 2 was worth the row — neither omission is a reaction to the record. Overall the record stands at 4/42 to target and -6.2% average, which is the context in which a report of seven position-management decisions and one accumulation bid should be read.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Eight ideas in, four out, every conviction score lowered, two mechanical defects in the report's own plumbing fixed.

THE ONE SYSTEMATIC FINDING: every one of the eight ideas counted `counter_argument_answered` as one of its distinct evidence kinds, and seven of the eight cite the SAME source URL as another evidence entry on the same idea. What those entries actually carry is a position-management rule - close first at 14.16, trim half into the print, refuse the trade above the SMA50, do not widen the stop - which is the idea's own technical_level or dated_catalyst restated under a second kind. strategy.md requires that kind be "answered with evidence rather than asserted away"; a rule is not evidence, and the same confirmation under two kinds is one confirmation. This is exactly the +1 that synthesis applied "mechanically" to six scores, and it is reversed: BCC 5 to 3, DKS 5 to 4, SIRI 4 to 3, ACM 4 to 3, OXY 4 to 2, TLT 3 to 2, HII 3 to 2. Three ideas lost a second kind on top of it - BCC's primary_document names the 10-Q and its filing date and then describes the following week's price action without quoting a single figure from the document, which is a filings-calendar lookup rather than a document read; DKS's counter-argument entry says in its own text that the case is only partially answered and cites a datapoint running against the thesis; and OXY's positioning entry (below both MAs while XLE rose six straight sessions) is evidence AGAINST a long and cannot also confirm one. No thesis was weakened by any of this and no level moved because of it - the evidence is what it always was, the scores now match it. Nothing is now above a 4.

TWO PLUMBING DEFECTS, both verified by merging this report against a COPY of state/open_positions.json rather than by reading the code. (1) BCC, the rank-1 CLOSE, published direction "sell" with catalyst.wait false. merge_report keys on (symbol, direction), and the live BCC position is a (BCC, buy) long - so the row did not close anything. It appended a 73rd position, a phantom (BCC, sell) short at 67.39 with no target and no stop that could never resolve, while the actual long stayed open at its 76.50 fill with stop null. An exit routed around the one-row-one-position rule by flipping the direction. catalyst.wait is now true, which writes no phantom row; the close itself has to be executed in the account and no field in this schema records it. (2) HII, whose entire stated action is "SET a stop at 278.50 where there was none", published catalyst.wait true - which makes positions_from_report skip the row outright, so the stop was never written. That position has carried stop null for 32 days through a 2026-10-30 amendment that also carried stop null, which is the same discard happening twice. Flipped to false, and re-verified: the amendment lands as stop 278.50 dated 2026-11-15 with the 262.00 entry and 339.76 target untouched, which is the filled-position rule holding. The four other holds (AAL, OXY, ACM, TLT) publish identical levels to the record, so their wait flags change nothing and were left alone.

ONE CUT: AAL, on the stop floor. 14.40 is 1.71 ATR from the 13.35 entry, inside the 2.0 swing floor, and the distinction that matters is that it was too tight the day it was set rather than walked in later - so the 2.62:1 was never a real ratio. The short stays open on its existing stop and stays first in the close-first queue; it is not republished. Synthesis predicted this demotion and it is the correct one.

ONE AMENDMENT THAT WAS MIS-DESCRIBED: DKS is published as amending the 2026-11-13 BUY with "the level unchanged". Only the entry is unchanged. The stop widened 132.25 to 129.00 and the target rose 170.00 to 175.50, so per-share risk is up 26% and the 2.00:1 clears the floor ONLY because the target moved out with the stop - at the standing 170.00 target the widened stop gives 1.65:1 and fails. Kept, because both new levels are better anchored than the ones they replace (129.00 sits below the lowest of the seven insider purchases where 132.25 sat in open air; 175.50 is the 45th percentile of the fetched 120-day range where 170.00 was a round number) and because the seven named-officer cluster is the only genuine one in 36 screened names. But the ratio is now disclosed for what it is on the row itself.

WHAT THE RED TEAM DID NOT FIND. Not one of this report's position-management decisions is wrong. Seven of the eight ideas are decisions about money already at risk, and all seven take the conservative side: no stop tightened, no stop widened, no target refitted, two positions explicitly queued to close first, and a stop finally going under the book's largest unprotected gain. Every cut recorded here is about scoring or about plumbing - never about a decision being the wrong one - which is why each cut note repeats the standing instruction rather than replacing it. The thinnest thing on the page is TLT, thin for a reason worth stating on its own: a long-duration thesis in a report that names rising real yields as the tape's single driver, with not one rate number fetched to test it because macro timed out twice.

RANKING. Conviction, then reward-to-risk, then catalyst proximity, renumbered 1-4 after the cuts recorded below. DKS takes rank 1 as the only conviction 4 - which also puts the report's one genuine new-risk idea at the top instead of an exit, though the two dated actions are unchanged and both fall on Monday 2026-11-16: close BCC at the open, trim half of ACM into the after-close print. BCC leads the conviction-3 band on that date rather than being sorted down for lacking a reward-to-risk ratio an exit cannot have.

THREE MORE CUTS, ALL ON THE SAME COLLISION, AND READ THE NOTES RATHER THAN THE COUNT. Scoring the evidence honestly put OXY, TLT and HII at conviction 2, where the 1% lottery-ticket ceiling applies - and all three are existing positions sized 2%, 2% and 3%. That ceiling is a rule about how large a thin NEW idea may be; it cannot retroactively un-size a position opened in September, and writing 1% to clear it would be a fabrication about money actually at risk. So the honest statement is that each position is now larger than its evidence justifies, which is a finding and not an error. Phase 2d would have demoted all three on that check anyway, with a reason that reads as over-sizing; they are moved here instead with the true reason and with each standing instruction carried into the note, because NONE OF THE THREE IS AN INSTRUCTION TO CLOSE. OXY holds on its unchanged 50.15 stop, second in the close-first queue. TLT holds on its unchanged 78.80 stop - do not widen, do not average down. And HII's instruction is the one that must not be lost: SET THE 278.50 STOP, in the account, because no row now writes it to the record.

SO THE COUNT IS FOUR RECOMMENDATIONS, NOT SEVEN, AND BCC MAKES IT THREE. Four of the eight published ideas are on the watchlist (AAL, OXY, TLT, HII) and BCC will join them at phase 2d on checks an exit row cannot pass - it has no target and no stop because closing a position has no reward-to-risk, and inventing either to clear the checks would be the fabrication the checks exist to catch. What survives on merit as a tradeable recommendation is DKS, plus two position-management rows with dated actions (ACM's trim into Monday's after-close print) or a resting order (SIRI's accumulation bid 11.5% under the market). That is a thin morning honestly counted. Worth saying plainly: seven of the eight ideas were decisions about money already at risk, and the red team did not find a single one of those decisions wrong - no stop needed moving, no position needed closing that was not already queued, and the one unprotected gain is getting a stop. What it found was scoring and plumbing: eight inflated conviction scores, one mis-described amendment, and two rows that did the opposite of what they said to the position record. Validation demoted 1 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 3 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.

Crypto was broadly risk-off with alts leading down: BTC -2.56% to 65,527 against ETH -4.12% and SOL -4.80%, so rising BTC dominance inside a falling tape is defensive rotation rather than a bid. recommendations.thesis: Seven distinct insiders - named officers and directors including CFO Navdeep Gupta, not a fund - bought 5.59M dollars of DKS across nine open-market purchases in September at 129.75 to 136.39, and the stock has since reclaimed both its SMA20 of 144.09 and SMA50 of 137.62 while sitting 38.7% below its 120-day high. Over the last month DKS has turned to outperform, up 6.29% against XRT at 3.68% and SPY at -2.26%, so the relative bleeding stopped roughly where the insiders were buying.
recommendations.key_risk: DKS has underperformed its own sector by 46 points over six months, down 30.85% while XRT rose 15.12%, which says the problem is company-specific rather than a cheap sector - and the two consecutive EPS misses, 3.53 against 3.801 for the September quarter and a 0.95% miss before it, are that problem. Earnings on 2026-11-23 sit inside the horizon, so a third miss gaps this through any stop; trimming half into the print is the only real mitigation. Short interest is unknown - the data source timed out - so no squeeze component is being claimed. AMENDMENT DISCLOSURE (red team): the 2026-11-13 row carried stop 132.25 and target 170.00; this one carries 129.00 and 175.50 at the same 144.50 entry, so per-share risk rises 26% from 12.25 to 15.50. The wider stop is the honest direction - 2.58 ATR, below the lowest insider purchase at 129.75, against 2.04 ATR before - but the 2.00:1 floor is only cleared because the target moved out with it: the widened stop against the standing 170.00 target gives 1.65:1 and fails the floor outright. 175.50 survives because it is defensible on its own terms, the 45th percentile of the fetched 120-day range where 170.00 was a round number - but read the 2.00 as a floor cleared by raising the target, not as an improved trade. Conviction cut 5 to 4: the counter_argument_answered entry says in its own text that the case is "only partially answered", and the datapoint it cites (analyst bullishness down 8.2 points, holds up 11) runs against the thesis, so it is not a fourth confirmation.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against: buying a name 30.85% lower over six months while its sector is 15.12% higher is textbook catching a falling knife relative to everything around it, analyst bullishness is down 8.2 points to 53.1% with holds rising 11 to 13, and net insider dollars are only about +1.0M once 4.58M of sales are netted off. The answer is structural rather than rhetorical: the stop at 129.00 sits below every one of the seven purchases, so the trade closes precisely where the best-informed buyers are proven wrong, the 1-month relative trend has already turned positive against both the sector and the index, and the 2.00 reward-to-risk comes from a stop set on the insider cluster with a target at only the 45th percentile of the 120-day range - not from a target chosen to clear the floor.
